Messages.Author: ramst...@my-deja.com
Messages.Body:
This came up in the last play session. Wasn't able to give a clear
answer on how to play the card after checking the errata. Requesting
clear definition on how the card is played. Is it Option 1, 2, 3 or am
I completely off-base here?

Option 1 - Card allows Malkavians to play Action Cards with Action
Modifiers while allowing Reaction Cards to be played in response to the
acting Malkavians (this includes the current Player)

Option 2 - Card allows Malkavians to take actions but without any
cards, Action or Action Modifiers. Other players would be able to
react to the actions the Malkavians are conducting and may use Reaction
cards with the exception of the player to whom the Malkavians are
piggyback riding their actions on. That player is unable to play
Reaction cards as it is still that individual's turn.

Option 3 - Card allows Malkavians to play Action Cards but no Action
Modifiers. Other players would be able to react to the actions the
Malkavians are conducting and may use Reaction cards with the exception
of the player to whom the Malkavians are piggyback riding their actions
on. That player is unable to play Reaction cards as it is still that
individual's turn.

Thanks

Michael Eichler

Sent via Deja.com http://www.deja.com/
Before you buy.

Messages.Author: James Coupe
Messages.Body:
On Tue, 7 Mar 2000 ramst...@my-deja.com wrote:
> Option 1 - Card allows Malkavians to play Action Cards with Action
> Modifiers while allowing Reaction Cards to be played in response to the
> acting Malkavians (this includes the current Player)

This one is close, but not correct.

The card allows Malkavians to take actions - and so allows them to use
action cards. An acting minion can always use action modifiers, so they
can play those too. Reaction cards can only be played by the vampires of
Methuselahs who aren't the acting minion, so anyone other than the acting
minion's Methuselah's vampires can play them.

So, if I use Dollface out of turn to call Kine Resources contested, I
cannot use my other vampires to play Surprise Influence to pass it.

--

James Coupe

> can play those too. Reaction cards can only be played by the vampires of
> Methuselahs who aren't the acting minion, so anyone other than the acting

Correct. Madness Network allows Malkavians to take actions during other
players' minion phases. It doesn't change any of the rules regarding those
actions, though.

The acting minion can play an action card [1.6.3.1] and action modifiers
[1.6.3.2]. Reaction cards can be played by ready untapped minions in response
to "an action taken by another Methuselah's minion" [1.6.3.5]

> So, if I use Dollface out of turn to call Kine Resources contested, I
> cannot use my other vampires to play Surprise Influence to pass it.

Correct.

First off the V:TES booklet is way out of date.

The official rulebook on the WotC site states the following about
actions/action modifiers/reactions in section 1.6.3.

1. Action and political action cards: A minion can play an
action card to take an action other than the default actions (default
actions are actions like hunt that don’t require a card). Only one
action card can be played for the action; action cards cannot be used
to modify other actions. Political actions are a special type of action
used to call referendums (votes). They can also be played for a vote
during a referendum (see Politics, sec. 6.3).

2. Action modifier cards: The acting minion can play these
cards to modify his action. For example, some action modifiers
increase the acting minion’s stealth or bleed amount, or give him
more votes. A minion cannot play the same action modifier more
than once during a single action.

5. Reaction cards: A ready untapped minion can play a reaction
card in response to an action taken by another Methuselah’s minion
(an action taken by one of a Methuselah’s minions cannot be reacted
to by any of her own minions). A minion cannot play the same
reaction card more than once during a single action. A reaction card
does not tap the minion using it.

----------
You will notice there is no reference any longer to who's turn it.

Hope this helps

Messages.Author: James Coupe
Messages.Body:
On Mon, 13 Mar 2000 tetragr...@my-deja.com wrote:
> I was refering as a poor card with the rule that
> a Methuselah can block, during its turn, acting Madnessed Malkavians.

If all actions taking during a Madness Network were unblockable, it would
be ludicrous. All it would mean was that I wait until the end of my
prey's turn and bleed him then, with them all unblockable. Add laptops,
pulses, etc. to taste.

> Victoria can be blocked or deflected or redirected as normal if she
> attempt to bleed just before your next turn.

Only the block would stop her. And Malkavians are well known for their
stealth. It doesn't matter who I bleed to get the edge, I still get it.

> It's a nice a well know trick this, but again, a not very strong
> one when a Methuselah can blocks a Madnessed Victoria in any turn.

Any time an acting minion takes an action, those minions who would
normally be able to block him can block him. It matters not whose turn it
is - the capacity for blocking is merely determined by who controls the
acting minion (for undirected actions) or who the action is directed at
(directed actions). That's how *all* actions work, whether under a
Madness Network or not. Is bleeding no longer a very strong
possibility? That's all the Madness Network deck is doing - it just adds
the capability for pool gain, making a strong deck stronger.

--

James Coupe

Two words: Night Moves. Works in an intercept deck too!

Also note that Victoria isn't even the one who has to bleed, so while
she can only Night Moves for +3 stealth, anyone with superior OBF can
do it for +6. Just as an idle note: the next-to-last tourney I
played in, I played my Tzimisce intercept deck. It lives or dies on
the "I can stop anything I don't want to happen" principle, packs a
TON of intercept, and does a lot of deal-making. I attempted to block
a hunt taken by my predator's Agrippina, who had a Laptop and Tasha
Morgan. She successfully generated +6 stealth manually to cover my +5
intercept, and I had used every different intercept card in my deck
(including Cat's Guidance superior). I didn't even BOTHER to go after
superior Night Moves actions. I've never known anyone to waste their
time attempting to stop superior Night Moves in an OBF deck, so
someone using it probably gets through, yanno?

-- Derek

>someone using it probably gets through, yanno?

Yes, massive stealth can be SUCH a major pain, even when playing an intercept
deck.

The best card to deal with this of course, is Veiled Sight. Even though it
costs 2 blood, at inferior level, it reduces stealth to nil. Suddenly it
becomes +0 stealth vs. +5 intercept. Of course they *can* still technically
increase stealth, but if you've played it right, they won't be able to because
of action modifier limits.

Seems ironic that one of the best intercept cards is in Chimerstry. Of course
the card is hamstrung by the fact that it IS a Chimerstry card (and who plays
Ravnos?), but it's still a possible (though not very feasible) option against
massive stealth.

Halcyan 2
